Occupational English Test
WRITING SUB-TEST:             PHARMACY
TIME ALLOWED:                 READING TIME: 5 MINUTES
                              WRITING TIME: 40 MINUTES

Read the case notes and complete the writing task which follows.


Notes:

Assume that today’s date is 15 May 2021. You work in a community pharmacy, and Ms King is a long-term client
of yours.
PATIENT DETAILS:
Name:              Ms Sarah King
DOB:               09 Jun 1979 (41 y.o.)
Address:           50 Sycamore Street, Newtown

Social background:
		              Married, 2 daughters (10 & 8 y.o.), call centre manager

Family history:    Sister – type 2 diabetes

Medical history: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) – since childhood		

Medication history:													
		               For SLE:
		                 -    Indometacin (Indocin) – since childhood
		                 -    Hydroxychloroquine sulfate (Plaquenil) – since childhood
		                 -    Cyclophosphamide (Cytoxan) – commenced 2020
		 -                    Prednisolone (Solone) – commenced 2020: dose Ógradually: 7.5mg/day in 2020 – 35mg/day
			                     now


Presenting complaint:
                Insomnia, SLE flare-up


Treatment record
08 May 2021
     Presentation: Routine – repeat script prednisolone (Solone) 25mg and 5mg

     Discussion: Pt complains: Óstress at work, Ótrouble sleeping, general fatigue, Ójoint pain, Óheadaches
                   Pt questions: steroids causing fatigue? Pt worried re side effects – long-term

     Diagnosis:    Stress Ò SLE flare-up

     Treatment:    Dispensed prednisolone with advice:
                   - Rest important Ò prevent SLE flare-up: time off work?
                   -   Reassurance – benefits of steroid treatment (Ôpain/swelling, Óquality of life (QoL))
                   - Regular moderate exercise
 
15 May 2021
Presentation: Request for over-the-counter sleeping tablet
				
Discussion: Appt with Dr 13 May 2021: Ófrustration & fatigue, trouble sleeping & exhausted during day
              Moody & irritable – short-tempered with children

                   Pt admits:
                   Anxious re long-term steroid use (making her ill?)
                   Dr insists Pt stay on steroid – warning: sudden prednisolone cessation Ò fatigue, weakness, 		
                   body aches

                   Pt’s decision: from 09 May 2021 Pt Ôprednisolone to 5mg 1x/day (Dr unaware) & Pt’s plan: 		
                   prednisolone cessation (against Dr’s advice) + start sleeping tab

   Diagnosis:      Long-term high dose prednisolone (>20mg/day) Ò insomnia

   Advice:         Pharm caution re sudden stop/re-start prednisolone (dangerous side effects)
                   Explain sleeping problem: high dose prednisolone (Òsleeping tablet not effective) – Pt’s consent
                   to inform GP
                   Declined dispensing sleeping tab

   Plan:           Write to GP:
                   Recommend review by Pt’s rheumatologist: comprehensive medication assessment




Writing Task:
Using the information given in the case notes, write a letter to the patient’s GP, Dr Smythe, discussing Ms King’s
medications and your recommendations. Address the letter to Dr Jo Smythe, Newtown Medical Clinic, 150 Station
Street, Newtown.
In your answer:
     ●     Expand the relevant notes into complete sentences
     ●     Do not use note form
     ●     Use letter format
The body of the letter should be approximately 180–200 words.
 
Any answers recorded here will not be marked.




                                                N K
                                      L A
                          B
 
PHASAMPLE05
Occupational English Test

WRITING SUB-TEST: PHARMACY
SAMPLE RESPONSE: LETTER




Dr Jo Smythe
Newtown Medical Clinic
150 Station Street
Newtown



15 May 2021



Dear Dr Smythe

Re: Ms Sarah King
DOB: 09 Jun 1979




                      TIAL
Your patient, Ms King, presented to my pharmacy today. I am writing to discuss her prescribed SLE medications and




                     N
recommend a review from her rheumatologist.




                  IDE
Ms King presented a week ago for repeat prescriptions of prednisolone (Solone) 25mg and 5mg. She complained of




                NF
trouble sleeping, fatigue, joint pain and headache, as well as increased stress at work. She questioned whether her




               O
long-term steroid use was causing her fatigue.




              C
I dispensed prednisolone and advised rest to prevent her lupus ﬂare-ups, suggesting time off work and moderate
exercise. I reassured her of the beneﬁts of steroid therapy for alleviating pain and swelling and improving quality of
life.

Ms King presented today requesting an over-the-counter sleeping tablet to treat her sleep disturbance. She admits
reducing her 35mg/day prednisolone to 5mg/day without your knowledge, from 9 May 2021, in an attempt to feel
better.

I suspect that long-term, high-dose prednisolone therapy may have been contributing to her insomnia; therefore, I
declined to provide her with a sleeping tablet. Additionally, I believe that a referral back to her rheumatologist for a
comprehensive medication assessment may be of beneﬁt.

Yours sincerely




Pharmacist
